To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iCLU and brain isoforms of BIN interact and that they both associate with Tau in AD.

(i) the intracellular form of Clusterin (iCLU) is up-regulated in the brains of Tau-overexpressing transgenic mice, but not amyloid mice, (ii) iCLU binds to Tau in cell culture and in human brain, (iii) iCLU and the bridging-integrator 1 (BIN) interact through their coiled-coiled domains in cell culture, and (iv) iCLU and BIN are associated with modified Tau in AD.

1) iCLU is an intracellular form that is upregulated in the brains of Tau-overexpressing mice, but not amyloid-overexpressing mice; 2) iCLU interacts with Tau and the brain-specific BIN1 isoforms; 3) iCLU and the brain-specific isoforms are found in association with modified Tau species in AD brains; and 4) expression of AD risk CLU variants leads to increased levels of the iCLU protein.
